item: The kill switch's refusal sentence is defined once and its readers are built from it
summary: The refusal 'network kill switch is active -- collection stopped by operator' was a literal at five raise sites in src/ingest/__init__.py and one in src/safety/fetcher.py, with the reader (fetch_verdict._OFFLINE_RE) and the law tracker each holding a copy of its opening words, so a rewording at one writer would have silently turned the operator's own refusal into a host failure. KILL_SWITCH_REFUSAL and KILL_SWITCH_REFUSAL_HEAD now live in fetch_verdict.py (which imports only re), every writer says the name, the regex's first alternative is built from the head, and law/track.py imports the head lazily. No behaviour change: the regex is compared with a frozen copy of the old pattern on 20 texts. 9 tests (AST scan for any other holder of the sentence, each of the six writers driven with the switch engaged, the reader equivalence), 11 mutants red. The reader is deliberately not widened for a Stop through an HTTP proxy (R320): that wrapped shape stays a non-match, pinned. Not a FetchFailed subclass (callers classify stored strings); the law tracker keeps startswith(head) rather than the predicate (a widening, stated). OSM granted the one-line fetch_verdict.py edit.
